A B Infrabuild is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor and RMC manufacturer. Its DRHP reveals heavy reliance on Western Railway, a shrinking revenue trend, and a working capital-intensive model.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild executes infrastructure contracts for government and PSU clients, primarily in the railway, bridge, and road segments. It also manufactures ready-mix concrete at its Thane facility.
Contracts are won through a competitive bidding process: the client floats a tender, pre-bid meetings are held, the lowest bidder is awarded the job after depositing a performance guarantee.

Major clients include Western Railway, Central Railway, Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd, and MMRDA. Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the order book.
Revenue is highly concentrated: top customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2018.
The company operates primarily in Mumbai and is expanding within Maharashtra. It uses box-pushing technique for bridge works and claims state-of-the-art machinery at its RMC plant.

business.heading: What the company does
business.purpose: Explain the business model, how it wins contracts, key products/services, customer concentration, and operating footprint.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations declined from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, a drop of about 33% over four years.
Net profit after adjustments was volatile: ₹0.96 crore in FY2014, ₹0.78 crore in FY2015, ₹0.33 crore in FY2016, ₹0.16 crore in FY2017, and ₹3.15 crore in FY2018 — a sharp recovery in the latest year.
Profit before interest, depreciation and tax (EBITDA) stood at ₹9.28 crore in FY2014, ₹9.46 crore in FY2015, ₹7.83 crore in FY2016, ₹6.76 crore in FY2017, and ₹9.29 crore in FY2018.

Long-term borrowings were ₹5.87 crore at end of FY2014, rising to ₹6.73 crore in FY2015, then dropping sharply to ₹1.89 crore in FY2016, ₹1.32 crore in FY2017, and ₹1.33 crore in FY2018. Short-term borrowings increased steadily from ₹30.82 crore in FY2014 to ₹35.37 crore in FY2018.
The company reported negative cash flows in recent years, though the specific figures are not extracted; the filing warns that sustained negative cash flow could impact business.
Total assets increased from ₹70.62 crore in FY2014 to ₹82.32 crore in FY2018.

financials.heading: Financial performance
financials.purpose: Present revenue, PAT, EBITDA, debt, cash flow trends across all reported periods with actual numbers in ₹ crore.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares, constituting 90.949% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.
Key management personnel include Ms. Anchal Pachori (CFO, aged 28, CA) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary, aged 26, ACS).
Directors' shareholding is negligible except for the promoter: Bharat Kumar Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh, and Mukesh Pandey each hold 300 equity shares.

Related-party transactions include loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors (₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018), director remuneration (₹57.7 lakhs), and outstanding payables to related parties (₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018).
Two companies promoted by Mr. Mishra — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited — were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 for non-operation.
No criminal cases have been filed against directors, and none are declared willful defaulters by RBI. However, the company faces pending litigation but details are not extracted.

beats.beat: The construction sector is highly fragmented and working capital intensive, contributing ~8% to India’s GDP. The filing cites an investment requirement of ₹50 trillion (US$ 777.73 billion) in infrastructure by 2022.
Growth drivers include government flagship programs (Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India), easing of FDI norms, rising urbanization, and India’s working age population projected to reach 64% by 2021.
The filing lists headwinds: slow pace of government projects, working capital crunch, and changes in government policies.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players. The company does not name specific peers in the industry section but provides a peer comparison in the valuation section.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor and ready-mix concrete manufacturer, promoted by Amit Bholanath Mishra. It operates in two segments: creation of infrastructure (railway, bridge, road projects) and operating a Ready Mix Concrete plant.

The company is raising capital through an SME IPO of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined, primarily to meet working capital requirements and for general corporate purposes.
The issue is managed by Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The issue comprises 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at an issue price to be determined. The filing does not specify an offer-for-sale component; the objects suggest a fresh issue.
Funds will be used to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and for general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed).
The lead manager is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
The company has not appointed any independent agency to appraise the project nor a monitoring agency for fund deployment.

offer.heading: The offer and its objectives
offer.purpose: Detail the issue structure, whether fresh issue or OFS, use of proceeds, and key parties.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the order book, and the top customers accounted for 57% of FY2018 revenue. Loss of this client would cause a significant revenue dip.

Dependence on government contracts: most revenue comes from winning bids from government departments. If bids are not accepted or are awarded at lower margins, financial condition will be adversely affected.
Negative cash flows: the company reported negative cash flows in recent financial years, which could impact its ability to fund operations and service debt.
High leverage: short-term borrowings have risen steadily from ₹30.82 crore in FY2014 to ₹35.37 crore in FY2018, increasing financial risk and vulnerability to interest rate changes.

Lack of independent project appraisal: the company has not appointed any independent agency to appraise the proposed project, and no monitoring agency for fund deployment, raising governance concerns.
